name: Split Jump
description: The split jump is a plyometric lunge variation in which the athlete is in a lunge position, jumps explosively, switches the legs in mid-air, and lands in the opposite lunge. It develops unilateral explosive leg drive, hip flexor and extensor power, and airborne leg switching coordination. The exercise is more demanding than a squat jump due to the asymmetric force production and landing requirements, and is commonly used in sport conditioning and circuit training.

execution.starting_position: Begin in a lunge position — right foot forward, left foot back, both knees bent approximately 90 degrees.
execution.setup_instructions: No equipment needed. Ensure adequate space and a non-slip surface.
steps: Step 1: Begin in a lunge position with the right foot forward.
Step 2: Explosively drive off both feet, jumping as high as possible.
Step 3: Switch legs in the air — left foot comes forward, right foot goes back.
Step 4: Land in the opposite lunge (left foot forward) and absorb through the ankle, knee, and hip.
Step 5: Immediately jump again, switching legs back to the starting configuration.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale sharply on each jump. Breathe during brief rest if pausing between reps.
common_mistakes: Not fully extending at takeoff before the leg switch
Landing with the front knee excessively forward past the toes
Collapsing the front knee inward on landing
safety_considerations: High knee stress — ensure good knee tracking in the sagittal plane.
Regress to static lunges then alternating reverse lunges before adding the jump.
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full lunge depth on landing — front thigh approaching parallel to floor. Full extension at takeoff.
execution.tempo_recommendations: Continuous alternating jumps. 10–20 reps (5–10 per leg) for conditioning; 6–10 for power.
coaching_cues: Front knee stays over the toes
